stem: Meera collects four samples during a school trip to a hill station. Her teacher asks: which sample is a mixture of different minerals rather than a single pure substance?

options.text: Quartz, a mineral made only of silicon and oxygen chemically joined together
Granite, a rock containing visible grains of quartz, feldspar and mica
Native sulfur, a yellow mineral found as the pure element near hot springs
Diamond, a mineral made entirely of carbon atoms bonded together

teacher.key_rationale: Granite contains several distinct minerals physically combined, so it is a mixture. Quartz (SiO₂) and diamond (C) are compound and pure-element minerals respectively, and native sulfur is a pure element; none of these is a mixture.
